sections.heading: 1. Reflection of Light
points: **Reflection** = the bouncing back of light from a surface.

sub: The **angle of incidence = angle of reflection**.
The incident ray, the reflected ray and the **normal** (at the point of incidence) all lie in the **same plane**.

points: **Regular reflection** — from a smooth surface (like a mirror), gives a clear image; **diffused/irregular reflection** — from a rough surface, scatters light (no clear image).

sections.heading: 2. Images and Multiple Reflections
points: A **plane mirror** forms a **virtual, erect, laterally inverted** image of the same size.
**Multiple reflections** between two mirrors form **many images**; the number depends on the **angle** between them.
**Kaleidoscope** (uses multiple reflections to form patterns) and **periscope** (uses two mirrors at 45° to see over obstacles) are based on reflection.

sections.heading: 3. The Human Eye

sub: **Cornea** (front transparent layer), **iris** (coloured, controls light), **pupil** (opening), **lens** (focuses light), **retina** (light-sensitive screen).
The **retina** has **rods** (dim light) and **cones** (bright light & colour); the image forms on the retina.

points: **Blind spot** = point where the optic nerve leaves the eye (no vision).
Care of eyes: enough light (not too dim/bright), don't look at the Sun/laser, eat vitamin-A rich food.

sections.heading: 4. Vision, Defects and Braille
points: Common defects: **myopia (short sight)** and **hypermetropia (long sight)** — corrected by **spectacles (lenses)**; **cataract** (cloudy lens, corrected by surgery).
**Braille** — a system of raised dots that lets **visually impaired** people read by touch (devised by **Louis Braille**).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Laws of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection; rays & normal in one plane.
Regular reflection (mirror, clear image) vs diffused (rough surface, scattered).
Plane mirror image: virtual, erect, laterally inverted, same size.
Eye parts: cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina (rods = dim light, cones = colour); blind spot.
Braille = reading by touch for the visually impaired (Louis Braille); vitamin A deficiency → night blindness.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Angle of incidence = angle of reflection** (measured from the normal).
The image forms on the **retina**; **rods** sense dim light, **cones** sense colour.
**Diffused reflection** happens from **rough** surfaces (still obeys the laws of reflection).
**Braille** was devised by **Louis Braille** for the visually impaired.
